short: A federation of Greek states created by Philip II of Macedon to unify Greece and facilitate the invasion of the Persian Empire.
full:
Following his decisive victory at the Battle of Chaeronea, Philip II summoned representatives from nearly all Greek city-states—with the notable exception of Sparta—to Corinth. There, he established a pan-Hellenic alliance, officially known as the "Hellenes," with himself designated as its hegemon (military commander).

The League forced an end to the endemic warfare among Greek polises by enforcing a common peace, while simultaneously co-opting Greek military forces into Macedonian service. It provided the legal and military framework for Alexander the Great's subsequent campaigns in Asia, effectively marking the end of the era of independent, warring Greek city-states.
